question: Should node-hosted agent tools receive trusted agent/session context so node skill reads can enforce the invoking agent's skill filter and remote eligibility, or should node skill context remain unavailable through this tool model?
rationale: The current params-only handler cannot preserve established agent-scoped skill policy, and choosing a trusted cross-node context contract changes the parent public API and disclosure boundary.

options.title: Add trusted invocation context
options.body: Extend the parent contract with server-derived agent/session policy context and require `node-skills` to use it for canonical snapshot resolution.

options.title: Keep node skills private
options.body: Do not publish agent-visible node skill tools until an existing or new scoped mechanism can safely provide them.

recommendation.title: Add trusted invocation context
recommendation.body: Extend the parent contract with server-derived agent/session policy context and require `node-skills` to use it for canonical snapshot resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: The parent invocation contract and current agent-scoped skill behavior both trace to this feature owner.
